indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the 'warns once' ADR-0095 invariant with the per-call logger.warning in render_markdown_to_wiki (dedup the warning or amend the ADR).
evidence: wiki_render.py:360-362 `pandoc = _pandoc_path()` / `if pandoc is None:` / `logger.warning(_FALLBACK_EVENT, extra={"reason": "pandoc_absent"})` fires on every render call
wiki_render.py:133-146 `_pandoc_path` docstring 'Deliberately NOT cached' — so every call re-probes and re-warns
docs/adr/0095-dc-segmenting-wiki-renderer.md:45 'Missing pypandoc returns the body unchanged and warns once'
test_wiki_render.py:250-261 test_dc_pandoc_absent_identity exercises a single render call, so the 'warns once across repeated calls' property is not asserted
indeterminate.finding: ADR-0095 invariant 6 states the renderer 'warns once' when pypandoc is missing, but render_markdown_to_wiki emits logger.warning on every call with no dedup/caching (and _pandoc_path is deliberately uncached), so once story 3388 wires it into the live send path a persistently-absent wiki extra would log one warning per rendered body rather than once.
scenarios: Story 3388 wires the renderer into a reconcile loop on a host without the wiki extra: every ticket body render emits a warning

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Align the 'byte-identical' wording with the strip()-based preservation check, or drop the strip so the check matches the claim.
evidence: wiki_render.py:280-286 `body = span.group("body").strip()` and `fragments.append(line.strip())` — fragments are stripped
wiki_render.py:266-271 docstring: 'must survive conversion byte-for-byte ... ANY rewrite ... is a content change'
docs/adr/0095-dc-segmenting-wiki-renderer.md invariant 1 'every code fragment of the source must reappear byte-identically'
indeterminate.finding: code_fragments strips each fragment before the preservation check (converted.find(fragment, cursor)), so the module docstring's and ADR's 'byte-identical' claim overstates the guarantee: leading/trailing whitespace of a code line/span is not part of the verified invariant.
scenarios: A conversion that only alters surrounding whitespace of a code span would pass the preservation check while the emitted code differs from source in whitespace

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the pypandoc-binary/pandoc (GPL) license and SBOM posture for the `wiki` extra, or confirm the deferral to story 5c0e is acceptable before merge.
evidence: pyproject.toml wiki extra comment: "`pypandoc-binary` BUNDLES the pandoc executable in its wheel"
docs/adr/0095: "Subprocess timeout, process-group reaping, safe-run batching, GPL/SBOM recording — story `5c0e`."

pandoc is distributed under GPL; the new wiki comment (unlike the adf comment which states `marklas` (MIT) / `mistune` (BSD-3-Clause)) records NO license for pypandoc-binary or the bundled pandoc — ABSENCE of license annotation.
indeterminate.finding: The `wiki` extra bundles the GPL-licensed pandoc executable (via `pypandoc-binary`), but license/SBOM compliance is explicitly deferred to a later story, leaving the current change with an unresolved license-provenance posture for a redistributed binary.
scenarios: Distributing rebar with the wiki extra installed pulls a GPL binary into the artifact without recorded SBOM/license attribution.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm pypandoc-binary==1.15 provides wheels for all supported dev/CI platforms, or add platform markers so resolution degrades cleanly.
evidence: docs/adr/0095 Platform section: "A platform with no wheel falls back to the identity path" and "`pypandoc-binary` also publishes Windows wheels."
pyproject.toml dev group adds bare `"pypandoc-binary==1.15"` with no environment/platform marker.
indeterminate.finding: `pypandoc-binary` publishes platform-specific wheels (bundling the platform pandoc binary); pinning `==1.15` in the dev group without a platform marker means the lock/install may fail or fall back on platforms lacking a wheel, an unverified provenance/availability risk.
scenarios: A developer or CI runner on a platform without a published pypandoc-binary 1.15 wheel resolving the dev group.

indeterminate.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a preservation test where the converted unit contains all code fragments but in reversed/swapped order, asserting the unit falls back to its source (guards the cursor's order-enforcement branch).
evidence: wiki_render.py:382-388 `cursor = 0` / `position = converted.find(fragment, cursor)` / `if position < 0: ... return text` / `cursor = position + len(fragment)` — the cursor advance makes preservation ORDER-sensitive

test_wiki_render.py:274-286 `test_dc_preservation_failure_returns_exact_unit` monkeypatches `_convert` to return "the code vanished" — a total-drop case only; a same-fragments-out-of-order conversion is never asserted
ABSENCE: no test injects a converted string that contains every fragment but in a swapped order, so a regression that dropped the cursor (making the check order-insensitive) would go undetected
indeterminate.finding: The renderer's preservation check enforces code fragments reappear IN ORDER (cursor advances after each match via `converted.find(fragment, cursor)`), but no test exercises a conversion where all fragments are present yet reordered; only the 'fragment vanished entirely' case is tested, so the order-enforcement branch is regression-blind.
